summary: This RFC requires Expert Review for additions to the part of the IANA XML Namespace and Schema registries that holds IODEF extensions. It was replaced by RFC 7970.

eli5.summary: Before a new item goes on the list for incident reports, an expert has to look at it first.

questions: do iodef extensions need expert review
how to register an iodef xml namespace
subtitle: Requiring expert review for IODEF extensions in the IANA XML registry.

tldr.problem: IODEF extensions were being added to the IANA XML registry without expert review to ensure compatibility with the base protocol.
tldr.mechanism: RFC 6685 requires Expert Review for additions to the IANA XML Schema registry for entries starting with 'urn:ietf:params:xml:schema:iodef'.
tldr.outcome: IODEF experts now review extensions before they are registered, ensuring they work well with existing extensions and the base protocol. This RFC was replaced by RFC 7970.

today: RFC 6685 is a Proposed Standard. It has been replaced by RFC 7970.

sections.title: IODEF Extensions and the Registry
sections.content:
The Incident Object Description Exchange Format (IODEF), defined in RFC 5070, lets incident response teams exchange information about security incidents. Extensions to IODEF can be added via class extensions in AdditionalData and RecordItem elements.

These extensions are registered in the IANA XML Namespace and Schema registries. RFC 6685 requires that in addition to IANA schema review, these registry requests must also be reviewed by IODEF experts to ensure the extensions are compatible with IODEF and existing extensions.
sections.eli5: IODEF is a format for sharing incident details. When people add new things to it, an IODEF expert checks them first.

sections.title: Expert Review Process
sections.content:
Changes to the XML Schema registry for schema names beginning with 'urn:ietf:params:xml:schema:iodef' are now subject to Expert Review. The IODEF expert or experts are designated by the IETF Security Area Directors.

The expert review ensures that new AdditionalData and RecordItem contents are correct and appropriate for IODEF. This is in addition to any schema review required by IANA for the XML registries themselves.
sections.eli5: The IETF picks IODEF experts. They check each new extension before it goes on the official list.

sections.title: No Direct Security Impact
sections.content: The document specifies no direct security considerations. The review process itself is a quality measure to ensure extensions are appropriate and compatible, reducing the risk of incompatible or insecure extensions being registered.
sections.eli5: The review does not directly address security, but checking extensions makes the system safer.
